arxiv-2108-11061.creator: Andrea Galasso, Chin-Yu Hsiao
arxiv-2108-11061.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Andrea Galasso, Chin-Yu Hsiao. Let ( X , T 1 , 0 ​ X ) (X,\,T^{1,0}X) be a connected orientable compact CR manifold of dimension 2 ​ n + 1 , n ≥ 1 2n+1,\,n\geq 1 with non-degenerate Levi curvature. arxiv-2202-08291.title: Microphysics of early dark energy
arxiv-2202-08291.creator: Vivian I. Sabla, Robert R. Caldwell
arxiv-2202-08291.description: Abstract Early dark energy (EDE) relies on scalar field dynamics to resolve the Hubble tension, by boosting the pre-recombination length scales and thereby raising the CMB-inferred value of the Hubble constant into agreement with late universe probes. However, the collateral effect of scalar field microphysics on the linear perturbation spectra appears to preclude a fully satisfactory solution.

arxiv-2206-15338.title: Rejuvenated accretors have less bound envelopes: Impact of Roche lobe overflow on subsequent common envelope events MESA ( Paxton et al. 2011 ; Paxton et al. 2015 ; Paxton et al. 2018 ; Paxton et al. 2019 ) , pyMESA ( Farmer & Bauer 2018 ) , POSYDON ( Fragos et al. 2022 ) , compare_workdir_MESA, Ipy
arxiv-2206-15338.creator: M. Renzo, E. Zapartas, S. Justham, K. Breivik, M. Lau, R. Farmer, M. Cantiello, B. D. Metzger
arxiv-2206-15338.description: Abstract Common-envelope (CE) evolution is an outstanding open problem in stellar evolution, critical to the formation of compact binaries including gravitational-wave sources. In the “classical” isolated binary evolution scenario for double compact objects, the CE is usually the second mass transfer phase.

arxiv-2302-04030.title: CrossCodeBench: Benchmarking Cross-Task Generalization of Source Code Models
arxiv-2302-04030.creator: Changan Niu 1 , Chuanyi Li 1 , Vincent Ng 2 , Bin Luo 1
arxiv-2302-04030.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Changan Niu 1 , Chuanyi Li 1 , Vincent Ng 2 , Bin Luo 1. Despite the recent advances showing that a model pre-trained on large-scale source code data is able to gain appreciable generalization capability, it still requires a sizeable amount of data on the target task for fine-tuning. And the effectiveness of the model generalization is largely affected by the size and quality of the fine-tuning data, which is detrimental for target tasks with limited or unavailable resources.

arxiv-2311-11807.title: Dissipation-based proper orthogonal decomposition of turbulent Rayleigh-Bénard convection flow
arxiv-2311-11807.creator: P.J. Olesen, L. Soucasse, B. Podvin, C.M. Velte
arxiv-2311-11807.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by P.J. Olesen, L. Soucasse, B. Podvin, C.M. Velte. We present a formulation of proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) producing a velocity-temperature basis optimized with respect to an H 1 H^{1} dissipation norm. This decomposition is applied, along with a conventional POD optimized with respect to an L 2 L^{2} energy norm, to a data set generated from a direct numerical simulation of Rayleigh-Bénard convection in a cubic cell ( Ra = 10 7 \mathrm{Ra}=10^{7} , Pr = 0.707 \mathrm{Pr}=0.707 ).

arxiv-2401-08416.title: Rings, shells, and arc structures around B[e] supergiants: I. Classical tools of non-linear hydrodynamics Journal: ApJ
arxiv-2401-08416.creator: Dieter H. Nickeler, Michaela Kraus
arxiv-2401-08416.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Dieter H. Nickeler, Michaela Kraus. Structures in circumstellar matter reflect both fast processes and quasi-equilibrium states. A geometrical diversity of emitting circumstellar matter is observed around evolved massive stars, in particular around B[e] supergiants. We recapitulate classical analytical tools of linear and non-linear potential theory, such as Cole-Hopf transformations and Grad-Shafranov theory, and develop them further to explain occurrence of the circumstellar matter structures and their dynamics.

arxiv-2409-12301.title: Amortized Variational Inference for Deep Gaussian Processes
arxiv-2409-12301.creator: Qiuxian Meng, Yongyou Zhang
arxiv-2409-12301.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Qiuxian Meng, Yongyou Zhang. Abstract : Gaussian processes (GPs) are Bayesian nonparametric models for function approximation with principled predictive uncertainty estimates. Deep Gaussian processes (DGPs) are multilayer generalizations of GPs that can represent complex marginal densities as well as complex mappings. As exact inference is either computationally prohibitive or analytically intractable in GPs and extensions thereof, some existing methods resort to variational inference (VI) techniques for tractable approximations.

arxiv-2410-15720.title: Efficient Non-Myopic Layered Bayesian Optimization For Large-Scale Bathymetric Informative Path Planning
arxiv-2410-15720.creator: Alexander Kiessling, Ignacio Torroba, Chelsea Rose Sidrane, Ivan Stenius, Jana Tumova, John Folkesson
arxiv-2410-15720.description: Abstract Informative path planning (IPP) applied to bathymetric mapping allows AUVs to focus on feature-rich areas to quickly reduce uncertainty and increase mapping efficiency. Existing methods based on Bayesian optimization (BO) over Gaussian Process (GP) maps work well on small scenarios but they are short-sighted and computationally heavy when mapping larger areas, hindering deployment in real applications.

arxiv-2504-12608.title: Code Copycat Conundrum: Demystifying Repetition in LLM-based Code Generation PubID: pubid: 0000–0000/00$00.00 © 2021 IEEE
arxiv-2504-12608.creator: Mingwei Liu, Juntao Li, Ying Wang, Xueying Du, Zuoyu Ou, Qiuyuan Chen, Bingxu An, Zhao Wei, Yong Xu, Fangming Zou, Xin Peng, Yiling Lou
arxiv-2504-12608.description: Abstract Despite recent advances in Large Language Models (LLMs) for code generation, the quality of LLM-generated code still faces significant challenges. One significant issue is code repetition, which refers to the model’s tendency to generate structurally redundant code, resulting in inefficiencies and reduced readability.

arxiv-2510-04187.title: A Complement to Neural Networks for Anisotropic Inelasticity at Finite Strains
arxiv-2510-04187.creator: Hagen Holthusen, Ellen Kuhl
arxiv-2510-04187.description: Abstract We propose a complement to constitutive modeling that augments neural networks with material principles to capture anisotropy and inelasticity at finite strains. The key element is a dual potential that governs dissipation, consistently incorporates anisotropy, and—unlike conventional convex formulations—satisfies the dissipation inequality without requiring convexity.

arxiv-2512-10834.title: Allometric scaling of brain activity explained by avalanche criticality
arxiv-2512-10834.creator: Tiago S. A. N. Simões, José S. Andrade Jr, Hans J. Herrmann, Stefano Zapperi, Lucilla de Arcangelis
arxiv-2512-10834.description: Abstract Allometric scaling laws, such as Kleiber’s law for metabolic rate, highlight how efficiency emerges with size across living systems. The brain, with its characteristic sublinear scaling of activity, has long posed a puzzle: why do larger brains operate with disproportionately lower firing rates? Here we show that this economy of scale is a universal outcome of avalanche dynamics.

pmc-11655773.title: Reporting guidelines for evidence‐based practice projects: A Delphi study and publication checklist
pmc-11655773.creator: Madeleine Whalen, Kim Bissett, Judy Ascenzi, Chakra Budhathoki
pmc-11655773.description: BackgroundEvidence‐based practice (EBP) is the cornerstone of sound patient care. Despite the known importance of disseminating EBP, of the 600 reporting guidelines registered with the EQUATOR network, none exist on reporting an EBP project. This lack of guidance leads to publications that lack rigor and discourages more novice writers who may not know where to begin.

pmc-11693227.title: WORK TOLL: AN INTERSECTIONAL ANALYSIS ON ABSENTEEISM AND PRESENTEEISM AMONG FAMILY CAREGIVERS FOR PLWD
pmc-11693227.creator: Mary Milnamow
pmc-11693227.description: Working family caregivers for PLwD experience higher rates of work productivity loss—absenteeism and presenteeism—compared to their non-caregiving counterparts. Accessible workplace supports remain out of reach for many caregivers making them vulnerable for compensation loss. Only recently has an intersectionality approach been used in quantitative research to address persistent inequalities across disciplines.

pmc-11713228.title: Virtual Reality‐based Cognitive and Exercise Intervention for People with Mild Cognitive Impairment. A systematic review and meta‐analysis
pmc-11713228.creator: Joyce YC Chan, Kelvin KF Tsoi
pmc-11713228.description: BackgroundCognitive training and exercise intervention are suggested for enhancing cognitive functions in people with mild cognitive impairment (MCI). The use of virtual reality (VR) has been applied in cognitive training and exercise intervention in recent decades. However, it is still unclear whether VR‐based intervention is a useful means to enhance cognitive functions in people with MCI.

pmc-12366160.title: Epidemiology and surveillance of influenza, RSV and SARS-CoV-2 in children admitted with severe acute respiratory infection in West bengal, India from 2022 to 2023
pmc-12366160.creator: Tila Khan, Ranjan Saurav Das, Abhishek Jaiswal, Sayantan Halder, Rina Maity Majhi, Arabinda Mahato, Tarapada Ghosh, Parthasarathi Satpathi, Sangeeta Das Bhattacharya
pmc-12366160.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundEvaluating the burden of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and influenza among young children in LMICs is crucial to inform implementation policies, given the importance of maternal influenza and RSV vaccination, which may not yet be widely available.MethodsThis study established a one-year surveillance of severe acute respiratory infection (SARI) from June 2022–2023 in hospitalized children 1–24 months from rural West Bengal India.

pmc-12428570.title: Impact of Novel Agents on Allogeneic Hematopoietic Cell Transplantation in Patients with T-Cell Lymphomas
pmc-12428570.creator: Yoshitaka Inoue, Jun-ichirou Yasunaga
pmc-12428570.description: T-cell lymphomas (TCLs) are generally associated with a poorer prognosis compared to B-cell lymphomas, and allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (allo-HCT) is often considered for eligible patients. One of the primary reasons for the inferior outcomes in TCLs has been the lack of effective novel agents for many years, resulting in a continued reliance on traditional cytotoxic chemotherapy regimens.

pmc-12642257.title: Loss of TET2 activity limits the ability of vitamin C to activate DNA demethylation in human HAP1 cells
pmc-12642257.creator: Maciej Gawronski, Marta Starczak, Aleksandra Wasilow, Tomasz Dziaman, Ryszard Olinski, Daniel Gackowski
pmc-12642257.description: BackgroundThe TET family of proteins—TET1, TET2, and TET3—are α-KG and Fe2+ dependent dioxygenases that play crucial roles in active DNA demethylation and the deposition of epigenetic marks such as 5-hydroxymethylcytosine, 5-formylcytosine, and 5-carboxycytosine. TET proteins can also oxidize thymine to 5-hydroxymethyluracil - a modification whose role is still poorly understood.

pmc-12722559.title: Characterizing approaches used to display antimicrobial resistance data in veterinary and human medicine: a scoping review
pmc-12722559.creator: Famke Alberts, Leilani Rocha, Emily He, Sheila Keay, Kurtis Sobkowich, Casey L Cazer, Scott Weese, Theresa Bernardo, Zvonimir Poljak
pmc-12722559.description: Introduction:Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a complex One Health problem that requires continuous surveillance to minimize the potential hazards. Information must be disseminated promptly in easily understandable formats to support informed decisions and actions by data end-users. One way to address this is through real-time visualizations, such as dashboards, to help key interest-holders understand and monitor AMR.

pmc-13190214.title: Learning curve, safety and diagnostic yield of the GalaxyTM, Noah Medical Group robotic bronchoscopy platform
pmc-13190214.creator: Lamia Aljundi, Ara Vartanyan, Tingyu Yang, Ching-Fei Chang, Shiqian Li, Monika Kakol
pmc-13190214.description: BackgroundNoah Medical Group (Reseda, CA) obtained Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approval for the robotic-assisted bronchoscopy (RAB) GalaxyTM System in 2023. The platform utilizes electromagnetic navigation (EMN) and integrated digital tomosynthesis (DT) for precise nodule targeting. Real-world data on its performance remain limited.

pmc-13364909.title: Examining the impact of generative AI on student motivation and engagement: the mediating role of autonomy-support and autonomous motivation in education
pmc-13364909.creator: Aldraiweesh Ahmed, Almutairy Sultan
pmc-13364909.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The rapid adoption of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) in higher education has transformed learning experiences; however, limited research has examined how psychological and motivational factors influence student engagement in AI-supported learning environments. Drawing upon Self-Determination Theory (SDT), Expectancy-Value Theory (EVT), and the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), this study investigates the relationships among perceived autonomy, competence, relatedness, expectancy, value, autonomy support for AI use, autonomous motivation for AI use, student motivation, and student engagement.

uslaw-usc-t21-s1902.title: 21 U.S.C. § 1902 — Purpose
uslaw-usc-t21-s1902.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t21-s1902.description: United States Code, Title 21 (Food And Drugs); Chapter 24 (International Narcotics Trafficking). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. The purpose of this chapter is to provide authority for the identification of, and application of sanctions on a worldwide basis to, significant foreign narcotics traffickers, their organizations, and the foreign persons who provide support to those significant foreign narcotics traffickers and their organizations.
